business_value.reason: The story identifies a specific beneficiary—the Stage 4 certification owner—and a clear outcome: auditable, safe, reliable end-to-end operation that qualifies the Story Analysis Workflow for certification. The analysis also names observable evidence such as agent quality scores, manual-correction and escalation rates, and an end-to-end success rate. However, the authoritative success formula, representative sample size, observation window, and treatment of human-resolved runs remain open, so the business outcome is not yet measurable enough for an exemplary score.
business_value.recommendation: Define the certification success metric, target threshold, sample size, workload mix, and observation window in the story. State explicitly whether human-resolved runs count as successful and what maximum manual-intervention rate is acceptable.

scope.reason: The analysis is detailed and bounded around Stage 4 certification, but it combines multiple independently deliverable workstreams: raising four agents to Stage 3 quality, adding several guardrail types, implementing ambiguity punch-out and signal authorization, creating atomic consolidated reporting, aggregating benchmark metrics, and producing certification evidence. It spans workflow orchestration, skill contracts, security, storage, evaluation infrastructure, reporting, and operations, with high complexity and unresolved ownership. This is an epic rather than a thin vertical slice.
scope.recommendation: Split the work into independently testable stories, such as: agent-quality certification evidence; startup and between-step guardrails; adversarial and post-grader guardrails; ambiguity punch-out and authorized human decisions; consolidated per-run reporting; and representative benchmark aggregation. For each story, define explicit in-scope and out-of-scope behavior and a single entry/exit outcome.

acceptance_criteria.reason: The eight acceptance criteria and thirteen dedicated edge cases are written in Given-When-Then form and cover happy paths, failures, permissions, ambiguity, reporting, business metrics, boundaries, concurrency, external-service failures, and partial writes. Most are directly translatable into tests. The criteria are not fully exemplary because several depend on undefined policies or thresholds—including the authoritative success formula, representative sample, authorization mechanism, timeout boundary rule, supported size limits, report lifecycle, and cost-unavailable representation—and some criteria bundle many assertions into one test case.
acceptance_criteria.recommendation: Resolve the policy questions and substitute concrete thresholds and deterministic expected outcomes into the affected criteria. Split compound criteria—especially input rejection, human-signal handling, consolidated reporting, and benchmark aggregation—into smaller criteria with one primary behavior each. Keep implementation choices such as atomic file writing as constraints unless they are themselves required observable properties.

story_format.reason: The story cleanly follows the required 'So that / As a / I want' structure. The goal is front-loaded, the certification-owner persona is specific, and the desired action names the exact gap categories to close. The persona journey, capability breakdown, and title reinforce a coherent and unambiguous narrative.

dependencies.reason: Dependencies are documented comprehensively across existing code, new code, infrastructure, external services, related stories, and required domain knowledge. However, the story is explicitly blocked by agent-quality work and unresolved stakeholder decisions about success semantics, representative evidence, adversarial review, signal authorization, cost treatment, retention ownership, and supported boundaries. These unresolved prerequisites prevent autonomous implementation and certification.
dependencies.recommendation: Assign owners and decision dates for every blocking question, record approved defaults, and identify which prerequisites are already available versus scheduled. Move independently deliverable blockers—especially per-agent Stage 3 remediation and any authentication infrastructure—into prerequisite stories, then narrow this story to work the team can complete with confirmed inputs.
